note:
Pelham Crescent read off the enumerators' pages for 1871, 1881 and 1891, transcribed by A. Hagues and checked by him line by line against a working sheet before import. The record already held eleven census rows for this street in 1871, fourteen in 1881 and twenty-one in 1891; what follows is the rest of the street, and it is the larger part by far.

**Four households in the record are fragments, and this mends them.** At 13 Pelham Crescent in 1881 the record had Edward Goldschmidt, one daughter and two servants, but not his wife or three of his daughters. At 5 Pelham Crescent in 1881 and again in 1891 it held only the servants and a visitor - the Flersheims themselves, whose house it was, were missing both times. At 13 Pelham Crescent in 1891 it held the head and two daughters but not his wife. Everyone bound by number here is bound to fill blanks, never to rename or overwrite.

**The 1871 schedule at 5 Pelham Crescent is not the Flersheims'.** The record has six 1871 rows filed at number 5 under Hermann Flersheim, but no Flersheim can be found in the 1871 returns at all, and the schedule for the house is William Hunt's, an attorney of 58. The Hunts are filed here at number 5; the six Flersheim rows the record still holds there for 1871 want unfiling by hand, since an import will not move what is already placed.

**Four houses the enumerator walked do not exist in the record.** There is no 2, 4, 6 or 8 Pelham Crescent among the properties, yet the 1891 enumerator wrote up schedules for 4, 6 and 8 in a continuous run between houses that do exist. Those three households are left unfiled with the address written out, rather than forced onto a neighbouring number.

**One house number is genuinely in doubt.** The 1891 schedule 6 can be read as 10 Pelham Crescent or as something else entirely, and both readings have support on the page. Its eleven people - John Henry Brown's household - are left unfiled until the number is settled, because filing them wrongly is worse than leaving them findable on the unfiled list.

**Pelham Cottage, Pelham Cottages, Thorn Lea and Lincoln Villa** have no property in the record either, so their households are unfiled under those names. Thorn Lea and Lincoln Villa are the sort of name that should eventually resolve to a number.

**An age that cannot be right is recorded as written.** Henry Meade Brown appears in 1891 as Son, aged 56, in a household whose head is 53. The age has been checked and re-checked and is what the page says. It is set down unchanged: the contradiction belongs to the schedule, and smoothing it away would hide the very thing worth noticing.
source: 1871, 1881 and 1891 census enumerators' pages for Pelham Crescent, Nottingham, transcribed by A. Hagues.
